title: Roos completeness of a constructible integral module in degree zero
statement: Let ell be prime, E/Q_ell a finite extension in any universe and X a Noetherian scheme. Every integral module sheaf C admitting finite constant constructible scalar models, placed in degree zero, is derived complete for SmallAdicCompletion: it has a K-flat representative P of C[0] for which the explicit positive-quotient Roos augmentation becomes invertible after localization. This says nothing about local models of arbitrary complexes, cohomology preservation or truncations.

source.place: Clause (2), Completeness, for a single constructible module

proof.text: Lift the canonical small field of E to the scheme universe by ULift. Uniqueness of the extended spectral absolute value identifies the two integer subrings. The induced ring equivalence is an isometry, hence a homeomorphism; postcomposition gives an actual isomorphism of the condensed ring objects. All these comparisons are constructed in the private helpers liftAbsoluteValue, liftMemIntegers, liftIntegers, liftIntegerHomeo and liftPointIso, with no existence witness left unproved.

Restrict along the inverse coefficient isomorphism. The existing constantModel_comap_iff preserves the constructibility hypothesis. Apply IntegralConstantModel.constructible_iff to obtain IsCompletedConstantStratified of the ordinary section-action realization, retaining torsion scalar models.

Apply the proved perfect_of_completedStratified helper of integral_cohomological_adic_criterion: a finite scalar module over the complete DVR has a finite free two-term resolution, which realizes the single complex. Its integralCoefficients helper supplies the DVR, completeness and unique maximal ideal hypotheses. The perfect-to-adic implication of adic_stratified_perfect gives local derived completeness. The exact functor comparison with singleFunctor transports this assertion to the realized original C[0].

Apply the general smallIntegralRoosCompletenessTransport comparison to the coefficient isomorphism and C[0]. Its local-completeness premise was established in step 3, and its conclusion is exactly the required explicit SmallAdicCompletion predicate.

theorem integralHeart_constructible_module_complete
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : Type v) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic ℓ) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic ℓ) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (C : SmallAdicCompletion.Modules ℓ E X)
    (hC : IsConstantModelConstructible
      (SmallAdicCompletion.Coefficients.integerRing ℓ E) X C) :
    SmallAdicCompletion.IsDerivedComplete ℓ E X
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj C)
